{{Lead too long|date=April 2021}}
{{Western name order|Meng Ling}}
'''Ling Meng''' is a Chinese [[Botany|plant biologist]] in the [[Department of Plant and Microbial Biology (UC Berkeley)|Department of Plant and Microbial Biology]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. She is currently a Postdoctoral Fellow at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. She is best known for discovering a novel form of [[cell signaling|cellular communication]] in plants.<ref>{{Cite journal| title = H Ekkehard Neuhaus: Faculty of 1000 Biology| journal = Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences| volume = 107| issue = 8| pages = 3900–3905| url = http://f1000biology.com/article/id/2426973/evaluation| doi = 10.1073/pnas.0913759107| pmid = 20133584| pmc = 2840455| year = 2010| last1 = Meng| first1 = Ling| last2 = Wong| first2 = Joshua H.| last3 = Feldman| first3 = Lewis J.| last4 = Lemaux| first4 = Peggy G.| last5 = Buchanan| first5 = Bob B.| doi-access = free}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> 
[[Thioredoxin]], while known to play an important role in biological processes such as cellular [[redox]], is not fully understood in function. Meng's work at Berkeley has suggested that thioredoxin h9 is associated with the [[plasma membrane]] and is capable of moving from cell to cell through two important [[protein]] post-translation modifications: [[myristoylation]] and [[palmitoylation]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Meng |first1= Ling |author-link1= Ling Meng |last2= Wong |first2= Joshua H. |last3= Feldman |first3= Lewis |author-link3= Lewis J. Feldman |last4= Lemaux |first4= Peggy G. |last5= Buchanan |first5= Bob B. |date= 2010-02-23 |title= A membrane-associated thioredoxin required for plant growth moves from cell to cell, suggestive of a role in intercellular communication |journal= [[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|PNAS]] |volume= 107 |issue= 8 |pages= 3900–3905 |pmid= 20133584 |issn= 1091-6490 |oclc= 60637487 |doi= 10.1073/pnas.0913759107 |pmc=2840455|bibcode= 2010PNAS..107.3900M |doi-access= free }}</ref> She is the first to connect [[thioredoxin]] with the [[plasma membrane]].

Meng received her M.A. in statistics in 2009 at the University of California, Berkeley.  She received her Ph.D. in Agricultural and Environmental Chemistry in 2011 at the University of California, Berkeley.{{cn|date=August 2023}}
